summary: Frontend-only testing of ASTEO weighbridge ticket PDF generator. Verified all fixed text is rendered, all 16 editable fields exist and are typeable, PDF download fires with correct filename and valid %PDF header (both custom and default), and Reset restores defaults.

ui_bugs.issue: Auto-grow width uses `Math.max(len,4)+1 ch`, but the handwritten (script) font in .tk-bl-input is wider than 1ch per char, so long values get horizontally clipped (scrollWidth 256 vs clientWidth 240 for a 15-char value). Default 'BL 9848' displays fine, but users typing longer references will see the last character clipped.

action_items: Increase width buffer for the .tk-bl-input handwritten input (e.g., multiply length by ~1.4 or use a canvas-based measurement) so long BL references are not clipped.
critical_code_review_comments: TicketDoc.jsx: width calc `${Math.max(len, min)+1}ch` only works for monospace/similar-width fonts. The BL input uses a script/handwritten font (see .tk-bl-input CSS) so 1ch under-estimates. Use a wider multiplier or measure text via canvas.
TicketMaker.jsx handleSave: filename sanitization replaces spaces and special chars with underscores. Acceptable, but consider preserving user intent or showing preview.
html2canvas at scale:3 produces a large ~4.6MB PDF for a small 80mm ticket. Consider scale 2 to reduce file size.

success_rate.frontend: 94% (15/16 fields render correctly + PDF + reset OK; 1 field has clip bug)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Pure client-side app. Frontend at REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Use Playwright with accept_downloads context to capture PDFs. All fixed text and 16 editable inputs verified; PDF download fires with correct filename (%PDF header confirmed). Only remaining bug: BL handwritten-font input clips beyond ~7-8 chars.
rca of the issue: BL input in TicketDoc.jsx sets width via `${Math.max(len,4)+1}ch`. The `ch` unit equals the width of the '0' glyph in the current font. .tk-bl-input uses a handwritten/script font where average glyph width exceeds 1ch, so the computed width is insufficient once length grows. Fix: use a coefficient (e.g. `(len+1) * 0.9em`) or a wider min (e.g. `+3ch`), or measure with a hidden span.
